content:
Apple TV+ is currently airing the fourth season of "Ted Lasso," with more high-profile series and films set to land on the streaming platform. Below is Apple TV+'s tentative fall slate, which may expand as more premiere dates are announced.

September

Mayday

  • Premiere date: September 4
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Action comedy

Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh team up for "Mayday," a genre-bending action comedy that completely颠覆s the spy thriller formula. US Navy top pilot Lieutenant Troy "Assassin" Kelly (Reynolds) is sent on a top-secret mission deep inside Russia at the height of the Cold War. When the operation collapses, he finds himself stranded behind enemy lines. Discovered by Nikolai Ustinov (Branagh), a stubborn KGB agent with a passion for American culture, Troy braces for the worst—only to discover that these two unlikely allies may ultimately lead to his rescue and strike up an unexpected friendship.

Last Seen

  • Premiere date: September 9
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Thriller

Detective Ian Ridley's (Patrick Brammall) life fell apart 11 years ago when his young daughter Maggie vanished without a trace. Now working as a police dispatcher, he is sustained solely by an unyielding refusal to accept that his daughter may be gone. When he receives a distress call from a young woman he is convinced is Maggie, he will stop at nothing to find her and reunite his shattered family.

"Slow Horses" Season 6

  • Premiere date: September 16
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Spy thriller

This darkly humorous espionage series follows a group of British intelligence officers who, after making career-ending mistakes, are banished to MI5's Slough House—a departmental dead end. Led by the brilliant but irascible Jackson Lamb (Academy Award winner Sir Gary Oldman), they navigate the smoke and mirrors of the spy world, determined to protect Britain from evil forces.

Brothers

  • Premiere date: September 23
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Comedy

"Brothers" follows McConaughey and Harrelson playing fictionalized versions of themselves. The longtime friends seem to have a great relationship—until they accidentally uncover a secret buried for years: they may actually be blood brothers. After his daughter calls off her wedding, Woody brings his entire family to Austin to stay for an extended period on Matthew's farm. What was meant to be a healing getaway quickly spirals out of control when Matthew's mother Ma Mac (Holland Taylor) blurts out the long-held suspicion that the pair might truly be brothers. Woody turns the farm upside down searching for the truth, while Matthew faces an identity crisis of his own: he may be running for governor of Texas. The result is a story that is both heartwarming and chaotic, packed with laughs, exploring friendship, family, fame, and the blurry line between myth and reality.

October

"The Last First: Winter K2"

  • Premiere date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Documentary

Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, "The Last First: Winter K2" examines the extreme climbing industry and its evolving culture in a complex, thrilling, and moving way. The story centers on a 2021 expedition featuring climber and Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson, along with Pakistani father-and-son duo Ali and Sajid Sadpara, aiming to become the first to summit K2 in winter—during the mountain's most brutal season. Along their treacherous climb, they encounter influencer climbers with their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and Nepali mountaineering legend Nims and his team of Sherpas. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers to the frozen heights of K2 with its unpredictable weather, unfolding a layered and surprising story of strategy and grit, class and hierarchy, money and power—all playing out in a life-or-death environment.

"The Sisters Grimm" Season 2

  • Premiere date: October 2
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Kids and family

Two sisters, orphaned, live in a town full of fairy tale characters, where they must battle heroes and villains while investigating the mystery of their missing parents. "The Sisters Grimm" weaves exploration, fantasy, and adventure together to deliver important messages to audiences of all ages.

"Small Prophets"

  • Premiere date: October 7
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Comedy

"Small Prophets" is a comedy about the eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley), who has been living a mundane life ever since his beloved Clea vanished seven years ago. He works at a hardware store and occasionally visits his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), all while desperately hoping for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe requiring rainwater, horse manure, and a dash of alchemy. Despite his doubts, Michael is determined to try brewing "homunculi"—magical sprites that can predict the future—hoping they will answer his biggest question: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

Matchbox The Movie

  • Premiere date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Action

Based on the classic Mattel toy line, "Matchbox The Movie" is a high-stakes, globe-trotting action adventure about a group of childhood friends whose long-lost former leader, CIA undercover agent Sean (John Cena), suddenly returns to their small town and inadvertently drags them into a wild international race to save the world.

Tenzing

  • Premiere date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Drama

"Tenzing," based on true events, tells the untold story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), became one of the first to reach the summit of Mount Everest. With encouragement from his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo) and support from expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe), they convince Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing should be a member of the British climbing team, not just a servant to them. Where Western climbers saw "Everest" as a peak to conquer, Tenzing revered "Chomolungma" as a sacred goddess of the mountains. The ascent that follows is shaped by the tensions of different backgrounds, classes, and ambitions, and fraught with the mountain's own dangers. But at the top of the world, empire, class, and ambition melt away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust—a lifelong dream and spiritual calling fulfilled for Tenzing.

"Where's Wanda?" Season 2

  • Premiere date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Dark comedy

Apple TV+'s first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about parents Dedo and Carlotta Klatt's frantic search for their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who disappeared without a trace months earlier. With the police investigation going nowhere, the family decides to take matters into their own hands, using surveillance equipment obtained with the help of their tech-savvy son Ole. Posing as utility company workers, they plant listening devices throughout the neighborhood and surrounding suburbs, only to discover that their neighbors are nothing like they seem behind closed doors.

Nocturne

  • Premiere date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Crime drama

The series follows Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), a former military man turned homicide detective who is burned out from the pressures of working the streets of Philadelphia and moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a quieter life. But when the town and his family are threatened by the sinister and calculating serial killer Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. When the search for Jurek's final missing victim forces Jonah to send his surrogate daughter, FBI agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), after Jurek, just how far will Jonah go?

November

"Stick" Season 2

  • Premiere date: November 4
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Comedy

"Stick" is a sports comedy series created by Jason Keller and starring Owen Wilson, who also serves as executive producer. Wilson plays Pryce Cahill, a former pro golfer whose career was cut short two decades ago, well past his prime. After his marriage falls apart, he takes a job at a sporting goods store in Indiana, pouring all his hopes and his future into a troubled 17-year-old golf prodigy, Santi (Peter Dager). "Stick" is a heartwarming, inspirational comedy about an unconventional chosen family and the bonds between them, set against a side of the golf world that has never been shown quite like this before.

12 12 12

  • Premiere date: November 13
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Heist drama

Each episode of "12 12 12" tells the story of a heist across three timelines: 12 months of planning, 12 hours of action, and the 12 days that follow. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) in a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the heart of the story is a heart-pounding bank vault heist deep in the streets of Zurich.

Being Heumann

  • Premiere date: November 13
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Drama

They wouldn't take Judy Heumann's phone calls, so she occupied their building. In 1977, a young disabled woman (Ruth Madeley) and a ragtag group of outsiders had had enough. What began as an impulsive action blossomed into the longest federal building occupation in American history—hundreds of people temporarily took over a government office, refusing to leave until the bureaucrats blocking their path (Mark Ruffalo) took action. They brought every form of rebellion into the hallowed halls of government, as the accidental leaders of a movement felt their way down a road no one had ever walked. Directed by Oscar winner Siân Heder ("CODA"), and based on real events, "Being Heumann" is a revolutionary, irreverent, and deeply human story about the most unlikely people attempting the impossible and changing millions of lives in the process.

"Way of the Warrior Kid"

  • Premiere date: November 25
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Action drama

Middle school has been a nightmare for Marc (Jude Hill)—he's a good kid, but he's bullied by his classmates and feels like he's falling behind in everything, from academics and sports to making friends. Everything changes when his injured Uncle Jake (Chris Pratt), a decorated Navy SEAL, comes to stay for the summer with him and his mom to recuperate. To help Marc protect himself, Jake devises an ambitious plan he calls "Operation Warrior Kid," modeled on his SEAL training. Rather than teaching the boy to fight, Jake shows Marc what real courage is, while also facing his own demons. Based on former SEAL Jocko Willink's best-selling novel and directed by McG ("Charlie's Angels," "Terminator Salvation"), the screenplay is written by Will Staples ("No Remorse," "Space Cowboys").

Apple may announce details of more fall titles in the coming weeks. But for now, that's everything that's been announced.

Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, and you can also save with a bundle through Apple One.
